title: Ya-Sin 36:61-64 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y10 lesson 35 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Ya-Sin 36:61-64 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 35. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: وَأَنِ ٱعْبُدُونِى ۚ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌۭ مُّسْتَقِيمٌۭ (٦١) وَلَقَدْ أَضَلَّ مِنكُمْ جِبِلًّۭا كَثِيرًا ۖ أَفَلَمْ تَكُونُوا۟ تَعْقِلُونَ (٦٢) هَٰذِهِۦ جَهَنَّمُ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ (٦٣) ٱصْلَوْهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ (٦٤)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: And that you worship [only] Me? This is a straight path.
And he had already led astray from among you much of creation, so did you not use reason?
This is the Hellfire which you were promised.
[Enter to] burn therein today for what you used to deny."

questions.q: Chunk and link Ya-Sin 36:61-64 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 36:61-64 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 36:61-64 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: What question does 36:62 end with, and why is it powerful?
questions.a: 'Did you not use reason?': it calls the listener to think.

questions.q: Find the two waqf signs in 36:61 to 62.

questions.a: A) Led astray a great multitude. 36:62.

questions.q: Ya-Sin 36:62: «وَلَقَدْ أَضَلَّ مِنكُمْ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: 'And that you worship Me: this is a straight path' (36:61). Why is worship called a 'path' rather than a single act?
questions.a: It is a whole way of life we walk every day, not one moment.
